Surah al-'Ankabut (The Spider) [Meccan, except from verse 1 to verse 11, which are Medinan] [It has sixty-nine verses; it was revealed after al-Rum]

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 2:

﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ That is, by their saying ﴿"We believe"﴾, ﴿and they will not be tested﴾, i.e., they will be tested by that through which the reality of their faith becomes evident. It was revealed concerning a group who believed and were harmed by the polytheists.

﴿And We certainly tested those before them, so Allah will surely know those who are truthful﴾ in their faith, with knowledge of witnessing (ʿilm mushāhada, knowledge gained by direct observation), ﴿and He will surely know the liars﴾ in it.

Or do those who commit evil deeds (al-sayyi'at), meaning polytheism and sins, think that they will outrun Us, that they will escape Us so that We will not take vengeance on them? Evil is what they judge: evil is the judgment they make, this judgment of theirs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 5:

﴿Whoever hopes﴾ (yakhāf, i.e. fears) ﴿the meeting of Allah, then the term of Allah﴾ (by which He is meant) ﴿is surely coming﴾ (fal-yastaʿidd lahu, i.e. let him prepare for it) ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ (li-aqwāl al-ʿibād, i.e. of the words of the servants) ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ (bi-afʿālihim, i.e. of their deeds)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 6:

﴿And whoever strives﴾ with jihad of war or of the self, ﴿it is only for himself that he strives﴾, for the benefit of his striving returns to him, not to Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ — mankind, jinn and angels — and from their worship.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 7:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾ by means of the righteous deeds. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best﴾ – meaning: the good (ḥasan). It is in the accusative because the preposition (bāʾ) has been removed (naṣabahu bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ al-bāʾ). ﴿Of what they used to do﴾, and that is the righteous deeds.

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾, meaning an enjoining that is good, namely that he be dutiful to them. ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾, by associating it with Me. The phrase "knowledge" here means knowledge that conforms to reality, so it has no implicit meaning (mafhum). ﴿Do not obey them﴾ in associating others with Me. ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾, that is, I will recompense you for it.
﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: [among] the prophets and the awliya' (friends of God), by resurrecting them with them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 10:

﴿And among the people is one who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people (i.e., their harm to him) as like the punishment of Allah﴾, out of fear of Him, so he obeys them and becomes a hypocrite. ﴿And if﴾ (the lam is a lam of oath) ﴿there comes a victory﴾ for the believers ﴿from your Lord﴾, so that they gain booty, ﴿they will surely say﴾ (the nun of the plural has been dropped from it because of the succession of the nuns, and the waw is the pronoun of the plural, for the meeting of two sukun), ﴿"Indeed, we were with you"﴾ in faith, so give us a share in the booty. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾ That is, He is knowing of their hearts, concerning faith and hypocrisy? (The answer is) yes.

And Allah will surely make known those who believe ﴿And Allah will surely make known those who believe﴾ [in their hearts], and He will surely make known the hypocrites, so that He may recompense both groups. The lam in both verbs is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 12:

﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way"﴾, our religion, ﴿"and we will carry your sins"﴾ by following us, if they are (the imperative is in the sense of the declarative), ﴿but they will not carry anything of their sins at all. Indeed, they are liars﴾ in that.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 29, verse 13:

﴿And they will surely bear their burdens﴾, meaning their sins, ﴿and burdens along with their burdens﴾, by their saying to the believers, ﴿"Follow our way"﴾, and by their misleading those who follow them. ﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾, meaning, they used to lie against God. It is a questioning of rebuke. The lām in the two verbs is the lām of oath, and the subject of both has been omitted: the wāw and the nūn of the nominative (ram).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 14:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people﴾, when he was forty years old or more, ﴿and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾, calling them to the Oneness of Allah, but they denied him. ﴿Then the deluge seized them﴾, i.e., the great water, which encompassed them and rose above them, so they drowned, ﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾, i.e., polytheists.

So We saved him, that is Noah, and the people of the Ark, those who were with him in it. And We made it a sign, a lesson, for the worlds, for those of mankind who came after them, should they disobey their messengers. Noah lived after the Flood sixty years or more, until the people multiplied.

(And) mention Ibrahim (Abraham), when he said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him," that is, fear His punishment, "that is better for you" than what you are upon of worshipping idols, "if you only knew" the good from other than it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, you worship, instead of Allah, idols,﴾ i.e., other than Him, ﴿and you invent a falsehood.﴾ You say falsely that the idols are partners of Allah. ﴿Indeed, those whom you worship instead of Allah do not possess for you any provision.﴾ They are not able to provide you with sustenance. ﴿So seek provision from Allah,﴾ ask Him for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 18:

﴿And if you deny⁠﴾ i.e., you deny me, O people of Makkah, ﴿then nations before you have denied⁠﴾ before me, ﴿and upon the Messenger is only the clear notification⁠﴾ — except the clear conveyance, in these two stories, as consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ).

**﴿Have they not seen﴾** with the ياء (ya') and the تاء (ta'), meaning **يَنْظُرُوا** (yanzurū, "look/consider"), **﴿how Allah originates the creation﴾**. The first letter of **يُبْدِئ** (yubdi'u) is pronounced with a ضم (damma), and it is also read with a فتح (fatha) as **بَدَأَ** (bada'a) and **أَبْدَأَ** (abda'a), with the same meaning: He creates them originating (ibtida'), **﴿then﴾** He **﴿repeats it﴾**, meaning the creation, just as He originated them. **﴿Indeed that﴾**, referring to what has been mentioned of the first and second creation, **﴿is easy for Allah﴾**. So how do they deny the second?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 20:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and see how He began creation for those who came before you, and caused them to die. Then Allah will bring about the final creation."﴾ [Say, to those who came before you, and caused them to die] ﴿Then Allah will bring about the final creation﴾, with madd (elongation) and qasr (shortening) and with the shin sukun (silent, i.e., pronounced with sukun on the shin), i.e., al-nash'ah (the creation/bringing into being) is read with an elongated or shortened alif, and the shin is pronounced with sukun. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾, and from Him is the beginning and the return.
He punishes whom He wills, [by] punishing him, and has mercy on whom He wills, [by] showing him mercy, and to Him you will be turned back, [that is] you will be returned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 22:

﴿And you cannot escape﴾ your Lord ﴿on earth or in heaven﴾ even if you were in it; i.e., you cannot elude Him. ﴿And you have no protector﴾ other than Allah, i.e., apart from Him, ﴿who could shield you﴾ from Him, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who could defend you from His punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 23:

﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and His meeting﴾, i.e., the Qur'an and the Resurrection, ﴿those have despaired of My mercy﴾, i.e., My Paradise, ﴿and those will have a painful punishment﴾, i.e., one that causes pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 24:

﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him."﴾ But Allah saved him from the fire into which they had cast him, by making it cool and safe for him. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, i.e., in his being saved from it, ﴿are signs﴾, namely, that it had no effect on him despite its magnitude, and that it was extinguished and a garden was produced in its place in a short time, ﴿for a people who believe﴾, who affirm the Oneness of Allah and His power, because they are the ones who benefit from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 25:

﴿And [Ibrahim] said: "You have taken only idols instead of Allah, out of mutual affection among yourselves in the life of this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others and some of you will curse others. And your abode will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers."﴾

(Ibrahim) — the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him.

(idols) — the things worshipped.

(mā) here is a masdariyya particle, meaning it turns what follows into a verbal noun: "mawaddata" (mutual affection) is the predicate (khabar) of inna. According to the reading in the accusative, "mawaddata" is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), and "mā" is a kafffa particle (one that prevents the governing force of inna from taking effect). The meaning is: you took them as idols out of mutual affection for worshipping them.

(in the life of this world) — the leaders (al-qādah) will disavow the followers (al-atbā') on the Day of Resurrection.

(some of you will curse others) — the followers will curse the leaders.

(your abode) — your final destination, all of you together.

(the Fire) — and you will have no (mani'īn, preventers) from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 26:

﴿So Lut believed him⦆ — he affirmed Ibrahim (ﷺ)... 

Let me restate precisely, following the passage as given:

﴿Then Lut believed him﴾ — he affirmed Ibrahim, and he was the son of his brother Haran. ﴿And he said﴾ — Ibrahim — ﴿"Indeed, I am emigrating﴾ from my people ﴿to my Lord﴾ — to wherever my Lord commands me. He abandoned his people and emigrated from the land of Sawad al-Iraq to al-Sham. ﴿Indeed, He is the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.﴾

And We bestowed upon him Isaac, after Ishmael, and Jacob, after Isaac, and We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book (bi-ma'na al-kutub, meaning the Books): namely the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Furqan. And We gave him his reward in this world, which is the good repute among all the people of the religions (al-adyan). Using the expression "sharai'" (the laws, sing. shari'a) instead of "adyan" is more precise and more fitting, because there is no true religion except Islam, and the religion of every prophet among the prophets is Islam; rather, the sharai', that is the rulings (al-ahkam), are what differ. And indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous (al-salihin), those who have the lofty ranks (al-darajat al-'ula).

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿Lot, when he said to his people: "Indeed, you﴾ [the two hamzahs in أإنّكم may be pronounced fully (tahqiq) or the second softened (tashil), and an alif may be inserted between them, in both forms, at both places] ﴿are committing the immorality (al-fahisha)﴾, i.e., the anuses of men, ﴿which no one among the worlds has committed before you," meaning mankind and jinn.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 29:

﴿Do you indeed approach men, and cut off the road,﴾ the road of travelers, by your act of committing the abomination with whoever passes by you, so that people abandoned the passage by you. ﴿And commit in your gatherings﴾ i.e., your places of conversation ﴿the evil deed﴾, the act of abomination, some of you with others. ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful."﴾ in denouncing that, and that the punishment descends upon its perpetrators.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 30:

﴿He said: "My Lord, help me against the corrupting people"﴾ by making true my words concerning the sending down of the punishment, ﴿against the corrupting people﴾ who disobeyed by having intercourse with males. So Allah answered his supplication.

ﷺ not present here. Translating the passage.

"When Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news" — [of] Isaac, and Jacob after him, "they said: Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town" — i.e., the town of Lot, "indeed its people were wrongdoers" — disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 32:

﴿Qāla﴾ [Ibrahim said], ﴿Inna fīhā Lūṭan﴾ [Indeed, in it is Lut]. ﴿Qālū﴾ [They said], i.e., the messengers, ﴿naḥnu aʿlamu bi-man fīhā﴾ [We know best who is in it], ﴿la-nunajjiyannahu﴾ [we will surely save him], with the lightening and the intensifying readings [of the verb], ﴿wa-ahlahu illā imra'atahu kānat mina l-ghābirīn﴾ [and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remain behind], i.e., those who remain in the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 33:

﴿And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed on their account﴾ — he grieved because of them — ﴿and felt helpless for them﴾ — his chest was constricted — because they were handsome of face in the form of guests, so he feared for them from his people, and they informed him that they were the messengers of his Lord. ﴿And they said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you﴾ — with the doubled and single letter forms (of the verb) — ﴿and your family, except your wife; she was among those who remained behind."﴾ The accusative of ﴿your family﴾ is a conjunction with the place of the particle of address (الكاف, "you") in ﴿save you﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 34:

﴿Indeed, We are sending down﴾ (read with light and with emphatic pronunciation) ﴿upon the people of this town a punishment (rijz)﴾, meaning a torment, ﴿from the sky, because﴾ of the deed ﴿they were committing defiantly﴾, meaning, because of their wickedness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 35:

﴿And We have certainly left of it a clear sign﴾ apparent, namely the traces of its ruin. ﴿for a people who reason﴾ who reflect.

We sent to Madyan their brother Shu'ayb, and he said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day﴾. [Fear Him], meaning the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And do not act corruptly on the earth, causing corruption﴾. This is an emphatic *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) whose governing verb is from ﴿عَثِيَ﴾ *ʿathiya* (with a kasra on the thāʾ), meaning "he corrupted" (*afsada*).
﴿So they denied him, and the earthquake seized them﴾ the severe quake, ﴿and they became prostrate in their homes﴾ kneeling on their knees, dead.

And (We destroyed) ʿĀd and Thamūd, with the sarf (the diacritic that makes them diptote-free, i.e., read with tanwīn) and leaving it unread means "the tribe" and "the clan." And it has become clear to you (their destruction) from their dwellings, in al-Ḥijr and Yemen. And Satan made their deeds appear fair to them, [such as] disbelief and sins, and so he averted them from the way, the way of truth, although they were discerning, possessors of insight.

﴿And﴾ We destroyed Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman. ﴿And indeed Musa came to them with the clear proofs,﴾ meaning the manifest arguments. ﴿But they acted arrogantly in the land, and they were not ones who could escape﴾ escape Our punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 40:

﴿Each of them﴾ from those mentioned ﴿We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a violent wind carrying pebbles﴾, a strong wind in which there were pebbles, like the people of Lut ﴿and among them were those seized by the Shout﴾, like Thamud ﴿and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow﴾, like Qarun ﴿and among them were those whom We drowned﴾, like the people of Nuh and Fir'awn and his people. ﴿And Allah would not wrong them﴾ by punishing them without a sin ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾ by committing sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 41:

﴿The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah﴾ i.e., idols, whose benefit they hope for, ﴿is like the spider's, which takes a house﴾ for itself, to which it resorts. ﴿And indeed, the frailest of houses is the spider's house﴾ weakest. It does not ward off heat or cold from it; likewise the idols do not benefit their worshippers. ﴿If only they knew﴾ that, they would not have worshipped them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 42:

﴿Indeed, Allah knows what﴾ (ma) here means "alladhi" (that which), ﴿they call upon﴾ (yad'una), i.e., worship, read with the ya' and with the ta', ﴿besides Him﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿of anything.﴾ ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 43:

﴿And these parables﴾ in the Qur'an ﴿We strike﴾, ﴿We make them for the people﴾ ﴿and none understands them﴾, i.e., comprehends them, ﴿except the learned﴾, those who reflect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 44:

﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, i.e., in a manner that is truthful (muhiqqan). ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, indicating His power, exalted is He, ﴿for the believers﴾. They were singled out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from it in faith, unlike the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 45:

﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿and establish the prayer. Indeed, the prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing﴾ legally: that is, it is of its nature to do so as long as the person is in it, ﴿and the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ than other acts of obedience. He explained the verse as meaning that the remembrance of Allah is greater than other acts of obedience. What the scholars have explained is that the remembrance of Allah through the prayer is greater than His remembrance outside of it, ﴿and Allah knows what you do﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 46:

﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ i.e., the argument that is the best, such as calling to God through His signs and drawing attention to His proofs. ﴿Except those of them who have wronged﴾ by waging war and refusing to acknowledge the jizya (poll tax), so argue with them by the sword until they embrace Islam or give the jizya. ﴿And say﴾ to those who have not yet acknowledged the jizya, when they inform you of something from their books: ﴿We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you﴾, and do not confirm or deny them in that. ﴿Our God and your God is one, and we are to Him Muslims﴾, obedient.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 47:

﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book﴾ — the Qur'an, just as We sent down the Torah and others to them. ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ — the Torah — such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and others, ﴿believe in it﴾ — in the Qur'an. ﴿And among these﴾ — the people of Makkah — ﴿there are those who believe in it, and none deny Our signs﴾ — after their manifestation — ﴿except the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the Jews. It had become clear to them that the Qur'an is true and that the one who brought it is truthful, but they denied that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 48:

﴿And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾ — i.e., the Qur'an. ﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾ — i.e., had you been a reader and writer. ﴿The falsifiers⁠﻿﻿﻿ — the Jews — would have doubted you, and would have said: What is in the Torah is that he is unlettered, who neither reads nor writes.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 49:

﴿Nay, it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an which you have brought, ﴿is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, i.e., the believers, who memorize it. ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., the Jews, who denied them after their manifestation to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 50:

﴿They say﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿Why not﴾, that is, why is it not so that ﴿a sign was sent down upon him﴾, that is, Muhammad, ﴿from his Lord﴾. In another reading (qira'a), it is "signs (ayat)" like the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Musa and the table (ma'ida) of Isa. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿The signs are only with God﴾, He sends them down as He wills. ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾, one who makes manifest my warning of the Fire to the people of disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 51:

﴿Is it not sufficient for them﴾ in what they requested, ﴿that We have sent down to you the Book﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿which is recited to them﴾? So it is a continuing sign, with no end to it, unlike the signs that were mentioned. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ Book ﴿is a mercy and a reminder﴾ an admonition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 52:

﴿Say: "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you."﴾ concerning my truthfulness, ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ And among that is my state and your state. ﴿And those who believe in falsehood﴾ which is what they worship besides Allah, ﴿and disbelieve in Allah﴾ among you, ﴿those are the losers.﴾ In their transaction, since they exchanged disbelief for faith.

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and had there not been an appointed term for it﴾ (determined by Allah), ﴿the punishment would have come upon them﴾ immediately, ﴿and it will surely come upon them suddenly, while they do not perceive﴾ the time of its coming.
﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment﴾ in the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 55:

﴿On the Day the punishment will envelop them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say﴾ In it (the verb) is read with the nun, meaning: We command the saying; and with the ya', (it reads) "yaqul" (he says), i.e., the one entrusted with the punishment. ﴿Taste what you used to do﴾, i.e., its recompense, so you cannot escape Us.

O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone. (Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 29:56): In whatever land worship is made easy for you, by migrating to it from a land where it is not made easy. It was revealed concerning the weak Muslims of Makkah, who were under constraint in openly displaying Islam there.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 57:

﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ Read with the (ta') and the (ya') [i.e., "you will be returned" (tur'ja'un) and "they will be returned" (yur'ja'un)], after the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 58:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely settle them﴾ We will lodge them. In another reading, with the letter "th" (ث) after the nun, from al-thawa' (ثَواء), meaning residence; and it is transitive to "ghuraf" (ghurfan) with the "fi" (in) removed: ﴿in lofty chambers (ghurafan) from Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally﴾ destined to eternal abiding, ﴿how excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ this reward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 59:

﴿Those who are patient⁠﴾, i.e., patient over the harm of the polytheists and over the emigration (hijra) for the sake of making the religion manifest, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely⁠﴾, so He provides for them from where they do not reckon.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 60:

﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision⦆ — how many (kam) of a moving creature (dābba) that does not carry its provision, because of its weakness, ﴿Allah provides for it and for you⦈ — O emigrants — even though you have with you no provision or sustenance. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing⦈ of your words, ﴿the All-Knowing⦈ of your inner thoughts.

The lam in ﴿and if﴾ is a lam of oath (لام قَسَم).

﴿And if you asked them﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?﴾ ﴿they would surely say, "God." So how are they turned away?﴾ i.e., turned away from His tawhid (affirmation of His oneness), despite their acknowledgment of that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 62:

﴿Allah extends provision﴾ He widens it ﴿for whomever He wills of His servants﴾ as a test; ﴿and restricts it﴾ He constricts it ﴿for him﴾ after the extension, meaning: for whomever He wills, as a trial for him; ﴿indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, and among that is the place of extension and restriction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 63:

﴿Wa-la'in﴾ the lam is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam). ﴿If you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and with it revives the earth after its death?"﴾ ﴿they will surely say, "Allah."﴾ So how do they associate others with Him? ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"All praise is for Allah,"﴾ for the establishment of the proof against you. ﴿But most of them do not reason﴾, [that is, they do not see] their contradiction in this matter.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 29, verse 64:

﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play.﴾ As for nearness (to Allah), it is among the matters of the Hereafter, because its fruit appears there. ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter—that is the (true) living,﴾ meaning life. ﴿If only they knew,﴾ that they would not have preferred the worldly life over it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 65:

﴿So when they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ That is, in supplication; that is, they do not call upon anything else along with Him, because they are in a distress that none but He can remove. ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.﴾ That is, in worship of Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 66:

﴿That they may deny what We have given them﴾ of blessing, ﴿and that they may enjoy themselves﴾ by gathering together in the worship of idols. In another reading, the lam is vowelled with a sukun (liyatamatta‘u), making it an imperative of threat. ﴿But they will come to know﴾ the outcome of that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 67:

﴿Did they not see﴾ (yaʿlamū, "did they not know"), ﴿that We made﴾ their land, Makkah, ﴿a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them﴾ by killing and captivity, apart from them. ﴿So in falsehood﴾ (al-ṣanam, the idol) ﴿do they believe, and in the favor of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ by their associating partners with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 68:

﴿And who⁠﴾ i.e., no one ﴿is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by associating partners with Him ﴿or denies the truth⁠﴾ the Prophet or the Book ﴿when it comes to him?⁠﴾ ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode⁠﴾ a dwelling-place ﴿for the disbelievers?⁠﴾ i.e., therein is that (abode), and he is among them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 29, verse 69:

﴿And those who strive for Us﴾ in Our cause, ﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾ i.e., the ways of journeying to Us. ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ the believers, with victory and help.
